Last molecule the budget can score. Ligand 1 is the acetyl probe and atom 17 its cyclopropane CH, bonded to the carbonyl at atom 15 - the lightest cap, and the one with the best SA. The thesis of this run is that the azine C4 position wants a flat aromatic ring: a phenyl there gave 0.70 where ten compact substituents all capped at 0.56 to 0.61, and the only obstacle is that a benzene takes the molecule past LogP 5 and destroys QED. Across this generation I have replaced it with pyridine, pyrimidine, pyridazine, methylpyrazole, methylimidazole, oxazole and isoxazole - a gradient from zero to two ring heteroatoms. This final call completes it with three: a 1-methyl-1,2,3-triazol-4-yl is the most polar flat aromatic I can put there, roughly two and a half log units below benzene, with no donor hydrogen of its own and no extra molecular weight beyond 334 Da. If the aryl effect survives that much nitrogen it is the most drug-like expression of the finding; if it does not, the gradient will show exactly where the effect dies, which is the more useful thing to hand to the next run.
